 Everett to be headquarters of Flukes parent company 

 Published 9:00 pm Thursday, October 8, 2015

   By Dan Catchpole and Jim Davis Herald Writers 

   Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...  

 EVERETT — The parent company of Everett’s Fluke Corp.

  Representatives with Fluke Corp. and its parent company, Danaher , could not be reached Thursday afternoon.

  Fluke, at 6920 Seaway Blvd., north of the Boeing plant at Paine Field, is a test- and measurement-equipment company that employs about 2,400 people worldwide. Danaher, with the stock ticker symbol DHR , is a Fortune 500 company focused on technology and based in Washington, D.C.

  Danaher announced May 13 that it was acquiring Pall Corp., a Port Washington, New York, company that provides filtration and purification services to remove contaminants from solids, liquids and gases. The deal was worth $13.8 billion.

  On the same day, Danaher announced that it would break into two separate companies, one focused on science and technology that would retain the name Danaher. Its revenue in the most recent fiscal year, including Pall Corp. revenue, was $16.5 billion.

  The second company would be a diversified industrial company that has been referred to as NewCo. That new company would include Danaher’s test and measurement businesses, such as Fluke, as well as its other specialty industrial businesses. The head of this new company is James A. Lico, a Danaher executive vice president.

  Danaher expected the separation of the two companies to be complete by the end of 2016.

  The city of Everett, the state and other economic leaders have been attempting to attract NewCo to locate in Everett. Economic Alliance Snohomish County interim CEO John Monroe said he would defer any comment to Danaher or Fluke about the companies’ plans.

**Because Danaher's common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker DHR, any brokerage account with access to US shares can buy it. The company behind the ticker has been reshaped more than once: it separated Fortive in 2016, Envista in 2019 and Veralto in 2023, then bought the patient-monitoring company Masimo in June 2026. What remains is a life sciences and diagnostics group whose 2025 sales were about 82% recurring, and this guide covers its three segments, the purchase steps and what its own filings say moves the shares.**

## What Does Danaher Do?

Danaher owns businesses that sell instruments, consumables, software and services to drug developers, research labs and hospitals. Its annual report calls it "a global science and technology innovator committed to accelerating the power of science and technology to improve human health," made up of more than 15 operating companies. Those companies sell under their own brands, such as Cytiva, Pall, Beckman Coulter, Cepheid, Sciex and Abcam.

The legal entity began in 1969 as DMG, Inc., a Massachusetts real estate investment trust, took the name Danaher in 1984 and reincorporated in Delaware after its 1986 annual meeting. The 10-K dates the idea behind today's company to the early 1980s and its founders, Steven M. and Mitchell P. Rales, who now chair the board and its executive committee.

The business reports three segments. **Biotechnology** sells what drugmakers need to develop and manufacture biological medicines, from monoclonal antibodies and vaccines to cell, gene and mRNA therapies; it was built on Pall, acquired in 2015, and Cytiva, the former Biopharma business of General Electric's life sciences division, acquired on 31 March 2020. **Life Sciences** supplies research tools such as flow cytometers, mass spectrometers and microscopes, plus antibodies, custom DNA and RNA, and industrial filtration.

## Executive Overview

Danaher is a Washington, D.C.-headquartered science and technology company focused on biotechnology, life sciences, and diagnostics. Its roots trace to 1969 through a predecessor company, with the Danaher name adopted in 1984. Over the last two decades, Danaher has reshaped itself from a diversified industrial group into a concentrated portfolio of healthcare and laboratory-technology businesses built around mission-critical tools, consumables, and diagnostic workflows. Its major operating companies include Cytiva, Pall, Beckman Coulter, Cepheid, Leica, SCIEX, Integrated DNA Technologies, Radiometer, Aldevron, and Abcam.

Danaher’s strategy is to own leading positions in attractive niches where customers value performance, reliability, regulatory quality, and ongoing service more than the lowest upfront price. A large share of revenue is recurring or repeat-driven because customers continue to buy reagents, filters, cartridges, antibodies, genomics inputs, service, and other consumables tied to an installed base of instruments and workflows. Danaher sells globally to biopharma manufacturers, research institutions, hospitals, clinical laboratories, and public-health customers. Following the 2023 spin-off of Veralto, Danaher is more tightly focused on life sciences and diagnostics. Fiscal 2024 revenue was approximately $23.9 billion.
